title: Agents, gateways and load balancing
summary: Where Collectors run (next to the app, or as a central tier), what each layer is for, and why tail sampling needs traces routed by trace id.

steps.title: Two layers
body: ```text
app ──OTLP──▶ agent Collector (same node)  ──OTLP──▶  gateway Collectors (a pool)  ──▶ backends
DaemonSet / sidecar / host               Deployment behind a load balancer
k8sattributes, hostmetrics,               tail_sampling, redaction, routing,
filelog, memory_limiter, batching          credentials for vendors, cost control
- **Agent** (one per node or pod): short hop for apps, adds host and Kubernetes metadata, scrapes local logs and metrics, buffers when
the network blips. Cheap, many of them, no global view.
- **Gateway** (a central, horizontally scaled pool): one place for policy (redaction, sampling, which vendor gets what), holds the
backend credentials so apps never do.
- Small setups run only one of them; the lab runs a single gateway. On Kubernetes the **OpenTelemetry Operator** manages both
(`OpenTelemetryCollector` resources with `mode: daemonset | deployment | sidecar | statefulset`) and can inject SDK auto-instrumentation.
**The tail sampling catch:** a gateway can only judge a trace if it has *all* its spans, but a normal load balancer spreads spans
of one trace across instances. So agents use the **loadbalancing exporter**, which hashes the trace id to pick the gateway:
```yaml
exporters:
loadbalancing:
routing_key: traceID
protocol: { otlp: { tls: { insecure: true } } }
resolver:
dns: { hostname: otel-gateway-headless.observability.svc.cluster.local, port: 4317 }

steps.prompt: Agent (next to the app) or gateway (central pool)?
items: `hostmetrics`: CPU and disk of this node
one redaction policy for every team

steps.prompt: Three gateway replicas run `tail_sampling` behind a round-robin Kubernetes Service. Errors are supposed to be kept 100%, yet many error traces in the backend are missing spans. Why?
options: Spans of one trace land on different replicas; each sees part of the trace and decides alone. Route by trace id (loadbalancing exporter) instead
The SDKs must use head sampling at 100% for tail sampling to work
steps.explain: The replica that holds the failing span keeps its part; the others drop theirs as "ordinary". The loadbalancing exporter with `routing_key: traceID` (and a headless Service so it sees every pod) sends a whole trace to one replica.

steps.title: Consistent hashing
body: Routing by `hash(trace id) % N` breaks when N changes: scale from 3 to 4 gateways and three quarters of the in-flight traces move,
split between the old and the new owner mid-trace. **Consistent hashing** moves only about 1/N of them. The loadbalancing exporter uses a
hash ring; **rendezvous hashing** (highest random weight) has the same property and fits in three lines: score every gateway with
`hash(traceId + gateway)` and pick the highest. Removing a gateway only moves the traces it owned; the rest keep their winner.

steps.title: Route a trace to its gateway
prompt: Write `string Pick(string traceId, List<string> gateways)` with rendezvous hashing: for each gateway compute
`BitConverter.ToUInt64(SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(traceId + "|" + gateway)))` (the first 8 bytes of the hash) and
return the gateway with the **highest** score (ties: the first in the list). With no gateways, throw `InvalidOperationException`.
solution: foreach (var g in gateways.Skip(1)) if (Score(g) > Score(best)) best = g;
hints: A local function `ulong Score(string g)` and a loop that keeps the best so far.
`MaxBy(g => Score(g))` also works and keeps the first on ties.
template: Dojo.Check("the same trace always goes to the same gateway", dojoIds.All(id => Pick(id, dojoGw) == Pick(id, dojoGw)), "");
var dojoCounts = dojoIds.GroupBy(id => Pick(id, dojoGw)).ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Count());
Dojo.Check("spread evenly (each gets 800 to 1200 of 3000)", dojoGw.All(g => dojoCounts.GetValueOrDefault(g) is > 800 and < 1200), string.Join(", ", dojoCounts));
var dojoMoved = dojoIds.Count(id => Pick(id, dojoGw) != Pick(id, dojoFour));
Dojo.Check("adding a 4th gateway moves about a quarter, not three quarters", dojoMoved is > 550 and < 950, "moved " + dojoMoved);
Dojo.Check("every moved trace moved to the new gateway", dojoIds.Where(id => Pick(id, dojoGw) != Pick(id, dojoFour)).All(id => Pick(id, dojoFour) == "gw-3"), "");
